quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 44

questions.question: If a train is near or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you must:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find an alternative route across tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing any railroad tracks. If a train is near or moving fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are not working.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you must:

options.text: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
Slow down without coming to a complete stop.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop completely at a stop sign. Check for pedestrians and cross traffic in the intersection. Wait for the intersection to clear before you go.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights warn of dangerous intersections. Treat them the same way you treat stop signs.

questions.question: Your blind spot is:

options.text: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
An area you can see in your rearview mirror.
An area you can see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Slow down and yield for trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield for trains.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead. Always slow down when approaching a railroad crossing. Trains cannot yield to cars, so you must let them pass before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?

options.text: Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the vehicle ahead is driving under the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Two solid yellow lines mean neither lane of traffic may cross them, except when turning into a driveway or business entrance. You cannot pass over a solid yellow line. No passing is allowed over solid yellow lines.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign is a:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow. In work areas, they may be orange. These signs warn you of hazards ahead or special rules in that area.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, a pedestrian should walk on the:

options.text: Same side traffic is moving on.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road that faces traffic coming toward them.

questions.question: When a vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes loses traction on a slippery road, you should:

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle loses traction on a slippery road, press hard on the brake pedal and hold it while steering out of danger. The Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) will pump the brakes automatically faster than you can. Removing pressure or pumping the brakes will turn off the ABS.

questions.question: A speed limit is:

options.text: The maximum or minimum legal speed under dangerous conditions.
The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions.
The suggested speed under ideal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the maximum or minimum legal speed you can drive under ideal conditions. You can drive slower than the posted speed, but driving faster is illegal. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, and when weather or road conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop and then go when the way is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
You can turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely. Wait until the light changes to green or a green arrow appears before you go.

questions.question: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train and then speed up.
Do what the car ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: Stop your car at least 15 feet from the railroad tracks when you see flashing lights. Look and listen for a train before moving.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, what should you do?

options.text: Always expect cars to stop for you in a crosswalk.
Do not enter the street when cars are coming.
Cross whenever you want because drivers must stop.
Use crosswalks only when it is convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter the street when cars are coming.
questions.explanation: Do not walk into a street or crosswalk if a car is coming toward you. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a close car may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is ahead. The road will split into two separate one-way roads. Stay to the right.

questions.question: What should you do when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Pull to the right side and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, pull to the right side of the road immediately and stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street the wrong way.
Do not drive in this lane.
Left-turning traffic must wait for oncoming traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-turning traffic must wait for oncoming traffic to pass.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers turning left on a green light to yield. Let oncoming traffic pass before you turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians are walking on the road.
Construction workers are on the road.

questions.explanation: This sign shows a pedestrian crossing ahead. Drive carefully in this area because people may be walking across the road.

questions.question: Roads freeze fastest when they are:
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze faster than sunny areas. Areas in shadow from trees or buildings are the most dangerous when it is cold and stay icy longer.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has many turns and curves.

questions.question: On a one-way street, when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights comes toward you, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the nearest side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down and let the vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the nearest side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Move to the nearest side of the road and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows an intersection ahead. A road is joining from the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They prepare drivers for road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign tells you a fire station is nearby. Watch for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped, yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign tells you a steep hill is coming. Be ready to adjust your speed.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a cell phone.

questions.explanation: Drivers need to focus fully on driving. Any extra activity can be dangerous and distracting.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, you should:

options.text: Depend on road signs to find your way.
Only have a general idea of where you are going.
Always choose the most direct route.

questions.explanation: Plan your trip before you drive. Check the location on a map before you leave. Do not drive to an unfamiliar place without knowing where you are going.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This one-way sign shows the direction all traffic must flow.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped, yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that wet pavement is slippery. Drive carefully and control your vehicle.

questions.question: Is smoking while driving distracting?

options.text: No, it does not affect driving.
No, it helps keep drivers alert.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving distracts you by taking your hands off the wheel or your eyes off the road.

questions.question: How can you reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use turn signals, obey speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.

questions.question: To be ready for hazards ahead, you should:

options.text: Look at the whole road and both sides.
Drive with your left foot lightly on the brake.
Look only at the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the whole road and both sides.
questions.explanation: Spotting problems before you reach them helps you handle dangerous situations. Do not just stare at the center of the road. Look at the entire road and the sides.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign means:

options.text: A reduced speed zone is starting.
The reduced speed zone has ended.

questions.correctAnswerText: The reduced speed zone has ended.
questions.explanation: Obey the school zone speed limit during the posted times. An "End school zone" sign shows where the reduced speed zone ends.

questions.question: Do not pass:

options.text: When school bus lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Never pass if there is oncoming traffic, if your view is blocked by a curve or hill, at an intersection, at a railroad crossing, on a bridge, or in any no passing zone. Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road with a median.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep tires at the correct air pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on water between the tire and road. Low air pressure and worn tires increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also increases this risk.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers what they must do. This sign is posted in parking lots. It marks reserved parking spaces for vehicles with a handicap sticker, tag, or license plate.

questions.question: You may drive around or under a gate that is going up or down at a railroad crossing:

options.text: If a train is not too close.
If your vehicle will not hit the gate.
If you look both ways carefully.

questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Wait until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully up before crossing the tracks. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic. Always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers who are already in the intersection.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs prepare you for road hazards. They are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you to watch for hazards and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You may honk your horn when:

options.text: You lose control of your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. Sound it to alert other drivers.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.

questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to dangers on the road. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: When you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend, you should:

options.text: Not worry about it because all vehicles are the same.
Hide from your friend that you don't know the vehicle.
Ignore any problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where the controls are and how to use them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where the controls are and how to use them.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, spend time learning where the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear shift, and horn are located. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: If a car is coming straight at you in your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Stay in your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.explanation: First, honk to get the other driver's attention. If they don't move, steer to the right. Don't steer left because if the other driver corrects at the last moment, you will still crash. Brake hard and steady. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the impact.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:
questions.explanation: Driving too fast on slippery roads is dangerous, especially in turns and curves. Approach turns much more slowly in slippery conditions than you normally would.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn drivers about construction zones. This sign tells you that the right lane will be closed due to construction. Be careful in these areas to protect both drivers and construction workers.

questions.question: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes. Where are they located?
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show you exactly where to stop.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles also yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: Always yield to emergency vehicles that are using sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: You reach an intersection with a flashing red light. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also coming to the intersection.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: What factors determine how much space you need to cross traffic?

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Whether you use your turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other drivers and road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other drivers and road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something others don't expect. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your hazard lights or horn when needed.
